pr.title: gvn: Invalid dereferences for all non-local mutations
pr.description:
Fixes #132353.

This PR removes the computation value by traversing SSA locals through `for_each_assignment_mut`.

Because the `for_each_assignment_mut` traversal skips statements which have side effects, such as dereference assignments, the computation may be unsound. Instead of `for_each_assignment_mut`, we compute values by traversing in reverse postorder.

Because we compute and use the symbolic representation of values on the fly, I invalidate all old values when encountering a dereference assignment. The current approach does not prevent the optimization of a clone to a copy.

In the future, we may add an alias model, or dominance information for dereference assignments, or SSA form to help GVN.

r? cjgillot

cc @jieyouxu #132356
cc @RalfJung #133474

issues.title: Panic in nightly 1.83.0 and 1.84.0 with opt-level >= 1 when unwrapping Some variant
issues.body:
When calling an unwrap on a value that *should* be Some, i instead get an unwrap on None error. Attaching a debugger seems to show an invalid memory error. This issue happens only when opt-level is set to at least 1, (aka in dev profile, no panic happens, and in release it does), and only happens in rust nightly 1.83.0 and 1.84.0, it does not happen on stable and nightly 1.82.0. ~~I'm not sure if the issue is in my code or in the sprs crate, i've filed [an issue](https://github.com/sparsemat/sprs/issues/370) there and also here just to make sure.~~ EDIT: managed to narrow down the bug by removing the sprs crate, this is only pure rust Here is the [repo for minimum example](https://github.com/Specy/microlp/tree/panic-bug) or in [the playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=0b00575c9057e816cddce89d00a0d856), there is an even smaller reproduction in the [comments](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/132353#issuecomment-2446804777) To reproduce, run `cargo run --release` which will panic, while if running `cargo run` it won't panic I've tried to run this with miri, nothing there. Also tried to run the release mode with bounds checking turned on, but nothing changed ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.84.0-nightly (3f1be1ec7 2024-10-28) binary: rustc commit-hash: 3f1be1ec7ec3d8e80beb381ee82164a0aa3ca777 commit-date: 2024-10-28 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.84.0-nightly LLVM version: 19.1.1 ```
Backtrace

``` thread 'main' panicked at src/main.rs:122:27: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value stack backtrace: 0: rust_begin_unwind at /rustc/3f1be1ec7ec3d8e80beb381ee82164a0aa3ca777/library/std/src/panicking.rs:665:5 1: core::panicking::panic_fmt at /rustc/3f1be1ec7ec3d8e80beb381ee82164a0aa3ca777/library/core/src/panicking.rs:75:14 2: core::panicking::panic at /rustc/3f1be1ec7ec3d8e80beb381ee82164a0aa3ca777/library/core/src/panicking.rs:152:5 3: core::option::unwrap_failed at /rustc/3f1be1ec7ec3d8e80beb381ee82164a0aa3ca777/library/core/src/option.rs:2008:5 4: microlp::order_simple 5: microlp::main at ./src/main.rs:152:5 6: core::ops::function::FnOnce::call_once at /home/specy/.rustup/toolchains/nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/core/src/ops/function.rs:250:5 ```

analysis.summary: GVN's old two-phase value numbering computed SSA values through `for_each_assignment_mut`, which skips side-effecting statements such as dereference assignments. As a result, a value derived from an immutable-reference deref `*r` could be reused after a non-local mutation to the same memory, producing a stale read (e.g. `Some` became `None` after `*v = None`). The fix removes the pre-pass and computes values on the fly in reverse postorder, tracking interned derefs and invalidating them (turning them into `Value::Opaque`) whenever a mutating place use with a non-empty projection or an unsafe terminator (anything other than `SwitchInt`/`Goto`) is encountered.
analysis.originalLogic: GVN first computed symbolic values for SSA locals in a separate pass using `ssa.for_each_assignment_mut(...)`, which iterates `assignment_order` and only visits direct assignments; it explicitly skips statements with side effects. The replacement pass then used the cached `VnIndex` of an immutable-borrow dereference `*r` (`r: &T`, `T: Freeze`) to replace later computations with a copy from that deref, without invalidating the cached deref on intervening writes through aliases.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Reusing a deref-derived value across a non-local mutation. The historical buggy MIR expected in `tests/mir-opt/simplify_aggregate_to_copy_miscompile.foo.GVN.diff` was: after `(*_1) = const Option::<i32>::None;`, GVN rewrote the result construction `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9);` into `_0 = copy (*_2);`, where `_2` was produced by `get(v)` and aliases `_1`. That reads the mutated location and returns `None` instead of `Some(col)`. The fix must not reuse the cached deref value after such a mutating use; in the new expected MIR the bad `_0 = copy (*_2)` is absent.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions where an SSA local holds an immutable reference to a `Freeze` type, a deref projection `*r` is used to compute a value, and then a non-local mutation that may alias the same memory occurs before that value is reused. Mutations include dereference assignments (e.g. `(*_1) = ...`), `SetDiscriminant(*v, ...)`, and non-trivial terminators such as `Call`/ASM. The representative program uses `fn get<T>(v: &T) -> &T { v }`, a `&mut Option<i32>`, `if let &Some(col) = get(v) { *v = None; return Some(col); } else ...`.
analysis.trigger: A deref projection `*r` through an immutable `&Freeze` reference is interned via `insert_deref`, then a write to a place with a non-empty projection (or an unsafe terminator) may alias the same memory, and GVN later reuses the interned deref value instead of re-reading/using the field value.
preconditions: The GVN MIR pass runs (e.g. `-O`/opt-level >= 1, or `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` in mir-opt tests).
A value is derived from a dereference of an SSA-held immutable reference (`&T` where `T: Freeze`).

A mutating use of a place with a non-empty projection occurs (`context.is_mutating_use() && !place.projection.is_empty()`), or a non-trivial terminator (anything other than `SwitchInt`/`Goto`) is reached.
The mutation may alias the memory observed through the earlier deref, so the cached symbolic deref value becomes stale.
pitfalls: Do not treat every deref reuse as wrong: after the fix, derefs are still reused inside uninterrupted regions (`tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` still expects repeated `Add` reuse for `let a = &z; opaque(*a + x); opaque(*a + x);`).

Invalidation replaces only tracked deref values with `Value::Opaque`; it must not disable all SSA reuse or the clone-to-copy optimization (`gvn_clone.rs` and `gvn_copy_aggregate.rs` now run without `-Zunsound-mir-opts`).
Only `SwitchInt` and `Goto` are safe terminators for preserving derefs; `Call` and ASM must invalidate derefs.
An aliasing write must actually occur before the stale reuse; merely holding `&T` or reading twice without mutation is not the bug.

Do not conflate borrowing restrictions with post-copy overwrite conditions, and do not treat a retained old test name/comment as proof that a replacement pass is correct; compare the actual value assignments.
The old tests were gated behind `-Zunsound-mir-opts`; the fixed expectations run by default and assert the absence of the stale deref copy.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/simplify_aggregate_to_copy_miscompile.rs` with an identity helper `fn get<T>(v: &T) -> &T` and `&mut Option<i32>`: match `Some(col)` through `get(v)`, then `*v = None`, then return `Some(col)`. FileCheck must see `(*[[v]]) = const Option::<i32>::None;`, then `// CHECK-NOT: _0 = copy (*[[v_alias_2]])`, then `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some`, then another `CHECK-NOT` for the stale deref copy. Add a custom-MIR `SetDiscriminant` regression: read `Field(Variant(*v_, 0), 0)` into `col`, then `SetDiscriminant(*v, 1)`, then return `Value::V0(col)`; assert GVN performs no stale-deref substitution (the before/after MIR remain identical). Re-run `gvn_clone.rs` and `gvn_copy_aggregate.rs` without `-Zunsound-mir-opts` to confirm clone→copy still fires. Use `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and, for the gvn suite, `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+InstSimplify-before-inline`, emitting MIR diffs with `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`.
